text:
elaine: quick heads up — after upgrading a customer from py-sdk 1.24.2 -> 1.26.0 they're seeing intermittent 401s and some customers reported being charged twice for the same request. rolling back to 1.24.2 stops the duplicates. anyone else hit this?

devin: can you share a minimal repro + logs? is it always on specific endpoints or random?

elaine: repro is small, happens on text generation and embeddings. snippet below. errors look like auth flapping followed by retries.

elaine: ```
# requirements.txt
redwood==1.26.0

from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate("hello world", idempotency_key="abc123")
print(resp)
```

elaine: log excerpt: ```
2026-03-16T10:12:32Z INFO sending request path=/v1/generate
2026-03-16T10:12:32Z WARN HTTP 401 Unauthorized (auth header missing?)
2026-03-16T10:12:32Z INFO retrying request (attempt=1)
2026-03-16T10:12:33Z INFO HTTP 200 OK
2026-03-16T10:12:33Z INFO request completed, charging customer
```

devin: that pattern would explain duplicate charges if the first attempt succeeds server-side but the client interprets it as a failure and retries. can you paste raw request headers (sanitized) from both attempts?

elaine: headers from failing attempt (sanitized):
```
Authorization: Token abcdef...
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: abc123
User-Agent: redwood-python/1.26.0
```
headers from retry that succeeded:
```
Authorization: Bearer abcdef...
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: redwood-python/1.26.0
```

elaine: notice the missing Idempotency-Key on the retry. we didn't change our code between attempts.

samuel: digging in. sounds like 1.26 changed some header aliasing/normalization. in particular we removed the old `Token` auth alias and consolidated to `Bearer` but there was an edge in the request pipeline that dropped the `Idempotency-Key` header when normalizing auth in some connection pooling paths.

maria: this has billing impact. please list affected customer ids and timestamps so we can start crediting. I opened a billing case and added INC-2026-4123.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4123. Assigned: @samuel, @devin. Priority: P1.

devin: short-term workaround for customers: pin to last known-good 1.24.2 (pip install redwood==1.24.2) OR set env var REDWOOD_LEGACY_AUTH=1 which re-enables the old header aliasing. We'll push a fix to the client and server.

samuel: confirmed. patch in client (restore idempotency passthrough and avoid header drop) will be cut as 1.26.1. server-side acceptance for both `Token` and `Bearer` auth will also be rolled out to reduce blast radius. targeting ship in ~3 hours after QA.

elaine: pinning to 1.24.2 fixed our immediate customer issue. we'll wait for 1.26.1 before upgrading fleet.

maria: billing will reach out to affected customers. please add the list of request ids and timestamps to INC-2026-4123.

devin: internal note: follow-up tasks — (1) add integration test for idempotency header preservation across retry paths, (2) add e2e test for auth aliasing, (3) publish advisory to #support + status page.

samuel: drafting the advisory now. will include the pin instructions, the workaround env var, and ETA for the patch.

elaine: thanks team — going to cc the customer and let them know we have an incident and a temporary workaround. :thumbsup:
